question.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{9-{x}^{3}}{2{x}^{3}+x}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

In this case, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{3}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{9-{x}^{3}}{2{x}^{3}+x} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{9}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{x}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{9}{{x}^{3}}-1)}{(2+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{9}{{x}^{3}}$ and $\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{9}{{x}^{3}}-1)}{(2+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & \to \frac{0-1}{2+0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-\frac{1}{2}.$
